## Personality

John Ashdown maintains a shy, distant exterior that hides a boyish heart, alongside a habit of mild politeness and occasional absent-mindedness. His primary ambition is to bring [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) to the old manse as his wife.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 CHAPTER XIV. MRS. ## History

In his younger years, John Ashdown was known as Jack and later lived at an ancient manse in [Juneford](../codex/places.md#juneford) with his late wife, Cecelia. While serving as a local minister, he became absorbed in reading [German](../codex/factions.md#german) theology to the point of neglecting his children, though he firmly rejected a proposal by Mrs. Hector Twiss to adopt his daughter [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md). Shaken by accusations regarding his parenting, Ashdown began spending time with [Clementine Ainslie](../character/clementine-ainslie.md), whom he eventually proposed to after encountering her in [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow). [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md) initially asked for time to consider, but due to a past vow made to her sister [Harriet](../character/harriet-ainslie.md), she ultimately sent Ashdown a cold written rejection that left him heartbroken. After [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) fainted at church from self-imposed fasting, Ashdown mourned his parental shortcomings and unresolved love for [Clementine](../character/clementine-ainslie.md), and later relented from whipping his son [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) after seeing his late wife's eyes in the boy.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER IX. IDA INTERVENES P87](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0087), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 CHAPTER XIII. ## Quotes

> “Mrs. Twiss, I am grateful for your good intentions,” Mr. Ashdown said with a courteousness that was gentle, decisive, and entirely terrifying, “nevertheless, my child cannot be given to you.”
>
> — John Ashdown — [v5 CHAPTER XIV. MRS. HECTOR TWISS MAKES A CALL P21](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0021)

> "Such a vista—such a perspective! Now and then I feel suffocated down in the Glen. Air is available to breathe up here."
>
> — John Ashdown — [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P21](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0021)

> "Extremely well done—truly, extremely well done. It hadn't occurred to me that you possessed such a combative spirit, Edmund."
>
> — John Ashdown — [v5 CHAPTER XVII. A DOUBLE VICTORY P67](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0067)

> "You received your small reprimand from me—and every one of you showed remorse—and you were forgiven by me."
>
> — John Ashdown — [v5 CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY P20](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0020)

> "To my mind, a day lacking wind appears lifeless. I am aroused by a windy day."
>
> — John Ashdown — [v5 CHAPTER XIII. THE HOUSE ON THE HILL P23](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0023)

### [Rupert](../character/rupert.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/john-ashdown--rupert.md)

John Ashdown is the father of [Rupert](../character/rupert.md), though he often neglects the boy due to his intense study habits.
